To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
demand for audit committees increases with total market capitalization and that audit committees have no significant effect on foreign equity investment.
the presence of an audit committee in a non-US commercial bank registrant is not a significant determinant of an increase in foreign equity investment.
demand for oversight and transparency protection in the sample US commercial banks is more like to increase as the size of the banks increase.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the adoption of audit committees for certain non‐US registrants and whether the presence of such a committee increases the transparency of the bank and its likelihood of attracting foreign investment.
the impact of audit committee oversight on the demand for oversight protection and foreign equity infusion.
the impact of audit committees on the likelihood of foreign equity investment for non‐US bank registrants (20‐F filer).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of an audit committee is a positive indicator of transparency, but the extent to which it affects foreign investment is inconclusive.
the presence of an audit committee for US commercial bank filers does not significantly influence the likelihood of non‐US commercial filers to adopt audit committees.
audit committees for US and non‐US commercial registrants have not yet been shown to be effective in increasing transparency and attracting foreign equity investment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the demand for oversight protection is not significantly affected by the presence of audit committee for the US and non‐US commercial banking firms.
the presence of an audit committee does not appear to significantly affect the likelihood that foreign equity investment will increase for non‐US registrants.
the presence of an audit committee does not appear to be a significant factor in increasing transparency for non‐US bank registrants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of an audit committee does not appear to affect the likelihood of foreign equity investment for our sample banks, but that demand for oversight in non‐US commercial banking registrants is more likely to occur as the banks increase in size.
the demand for audit committee oversight protection is not necessarily a significant factor in the decision to adopt audit committees.
audit committees for non-US commercial banks are not a substitute for the presence of a strong corporate governance structure.
